title.narrative: ROAP/AFG01/25/Data Collection Survey on the Kabul Solidarity Programme (KSP)

description.narrative:
The Data Collection Survey (later referenced as “the Survey”) focuses on one selected area (PD16) out of the four PDs originally covered by the Kabul Solidarity Programme (KSP) (later called “the project”), a sub-programme of the Kabul Metropolitan Development Project (2010-2015). Implemented from July 2013 to November 2014 (17 months), KSP Phase II (KSP2) was a collaboration between JICA and UN-Habitat, with a project value of USD 5.4 million. The programme made notable progress in community-led development and infrastructure strengthening within informal settlements in Kabul.
KSP prioritized upgrading urban informal settlements by actively engaging communities. With Kabul experiencing a significant population influx due to multifaceted crises and rural-urban migration, KSP addressed critical infrastructure and service needs. The project established 24 Neighbourhood Development Councils (NDCs) and 7 Gozar Development Councils (GDCs) across four police districts (PDs 4, 11, 12, and 16), developing Community Action Plans (CAPs) to guide local development. KSP2 successfully completed 31 community-led sub-projects—24 at the community level and 7 at the Gozar level—benefiting 4,391 households and 51,703 individuals.
However, since the de facto government’s takeover in August 2021, Afghanistan has faced severe economic decline, widespread poverty, and disruption of essential public services. Women’s rights and participation in socio-economic activities have been strictly limited. In 2024, the de facto authorities (DFA) ordered the dismantling of established community structures, further restricting community participation in decision-making processes.
Against this backdrop, the Survey aims to assess the impact of KSP2 after ten years, collect updated information on community structures, and identify trends in urban development, particularly community-led initiatives and infrastructure upgrading – focusing on ONE OF THE FOUR original PDs (PD16). As part of the Survey, pilot activities, including refresher training sessions for community representatives to reinforce participatory approaches in identifying community needs and developing action plans for settlement improvement, will also be conducted.
The findings of the Survey will help refine strategic approaches and support the effective implementation of similar projects, including “The Project for the Improvement of Living Environment for Vulnerable People in Urban Areas,” a collaboration between UN-Habitat and JICA, as well as impact UN-Habitat’s programming for Afghanistan.
